title: The Last Ember Anew
premise: Ada Dravenmoor has spent his life as the royal food-taster of Vell Hollow, a valley where magic cannot enter, swallowing poison in small doses so his body becomes a living shield for the king. When a mute child arrives at the palace gates speaking a language older than any kingdom, Ada alone can understand him — and learns the child's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain, where magic reigns and time runs differently. To save him, Ada must leave the valley that made him safe, trading his immunity for vulnerability as he infiltrates the subterranean court with the help of Sera, an exiled ember-keeper who once loved him and now serves his enemy. In the end, Ada discovers the child is the last ember of the valley's founding magic, and he must choose between returning home whole or burning himself out to rekindle it — choosing love and belonging over duty, at the cost of everything he was.
about_author: Gideon Zhou is a former line cook who spent six years working in hotel kitchens before turning to fantasy, a background that infuses his fiction with an obsessive attention to food, ritual, and the quiet violence of service. He lives near a river valley and writes at night, claiming the dark helps him hear old languages better.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We open on a morning tasting: bitter almond hidden in the king's honeyed porridge, Ada's trained tongue catching death by habit. Establishes his numb pride, his immunity built dish by dish, and the valley's rule — magic cannot cross its borders. Emotional beat: competence masking emptiness; Ada has never wanted anything enough to risk it.

chapters.title: A Knock Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A child appears at the servants' gate at dusk, barefoot, unafraid, speaking a language no scholar in the palace recognizes — but Ada understands him, word for word, though he cannot say why. The child, Wren, will not eat until Ada tastes the food first. Emotional beat: recognition without explanation; something long asleep in Ada stirs.

chapters.title: What the King Cannot Know
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with a brief interlude from Chancellor Merek. Ada hides Wren in the taster's quarters while the court debates sending the child to the border priests. Merek suspects the boy is a magical thing smuggled in — impossible, in a valley where magic cannot follow. Emotional beat: first loyalty conflict; Ada lies to the crown for the first time in his life.

chapters.title: The Language Beneath Words
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Nights spent teaching Wren kitchen words; Wren draws spirals and mountains and a door under stone. Through fragments, Ada grasps the horror: Wren's soul was sold, and the buyers live beneath the mountain, beyond the valley's edge. Emotional beat: tenderness deepening into purpose; Ada begins wanting something worth risking.

chapters.title: Sera at the Border Stone
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. At the valley's edge stands the border stone where magic stops. Sera, an exiled ember-keeper, waits there because she felt the child cross — felt the valley itself shudder. She remembers Ada, the man she loved before her exile, and knows he'll come. Emotional beat: longing sharpened by resentment; she has counted the years.

chapters.title: Poison Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The king falls mysteriously ill despite Ada's tastings — poison that isn't poison but curse-work, which means someone inside the valley is serving the mountain court. Merek accuses Wren. Emotional beat: dread and betrayal; the safe valley was never safe, and Ada's immunity is useless against this.

chapters.title: The Price of Leaving
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada decides to take Wren out through the border stone. Crossing it feels like drowning — magic floods back into a body built to resist poison, not enchantment, and every old immunity burns like swallowed coals. Sera finds them collapsed on the far side. Emotional beat: sacrifice made real; leaving costs him the self he was.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and Sera POV. The three travel toward the mountain through country where roads rearrange themselves overnight. Old wounds reopen between Ada and Sera — why she was exiled, what she chose over him. Wren watches them fight in his borrowed language. Emotional beat: bitterness curdling into honesty; love against duty takes sides.

chapters.title: The Inn of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Shelter at an inn whose keeper trades in memories instead of coin. Sera sells a memory of her mother to buy passage information; Ada offers a memory of the king he served, and finds he doesn't miss it. Emotional beat: grief and lightness entwined; they learn what they're willing to lose.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Merek's riders catch up — the chancellor serves the mountain court and wants Wren's soul-contract enforced. A night skirmish; Ada's poisoned blood, thickened by years of immunity, turns out to be lethal to the hunters' magic. Emotional beat: fierce protectiveness; Ada discovers his damage is also a weapon.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They descend through the mountain's throat into a court lit by cold fire, where nobles wear centuries like jewelry and bargains are the only law. Sera is recognized — and hated. Emotional beat: awe laced with terror; beauty here is a trap with excellent manners.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada petitions the court for Wren's soul. The Lord Under the Mountain agrees to hear terms — but demands a taster's service first: Ada must eat at the court's table for nine nights, testing dishes brewed with intent, while Sera negotiates separately. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in ceremony; every meal is a negotiation he can't read.

chapters.title: Nine Nights, First Three
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The early feasts: dishes of forgetting, of obedience, of false homesickness. Ada's immunity holds against some, fails against others — one night he weeps for a childhood that wasn't his. Wren grows paler as the contract tightens. Emotional beat: erosion; the court is patient and Ada is not.

chapters.title: What Sera Sold
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Revealed: Sera's exile came from refusing to feed the court's ember-fires years ago, and the Lord offers her reinstatement if she delivers Wren alone. She refuses again — but hides the refusal from Ada, ashamed of how tempted she was. Emotional beat: guilt and loyalty at war; truth deferred is a debt accruing interest.

chapters.title: Nights Four Through Six
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The middle feasts turn intimate — the court serves Ada his own memories, plated beautifully: the king's kindness, the valley's safety, Sera's face at nineteen. He realizes the court is studying what he loves to price what he'll pay. Emotional beat: exposure; love mapped and weaponized.

chapters.title: The Ember Truth
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera learns Wren is not merely a child with a sold soul — he IS the last ember of the valley's founding magic, embodied, and the court bought him to extinguish the valley forever. The 'illness' of the king, Merek's treason, all of it was kindling. Emotional beat: revelation as vertigo; the stakes were never one child.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Seventh Table
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Merek arrives as the court's honored guest and reveals Sera's secret negotiations — that she considered the offer, that she hid things. The court offers Ada a final bargain: his own soul for Wren's freedom. Ada, hollowed by seven feasts, nearly says yes. Emotional beat: betrayal's sting and its cure — Ada chooses trust anyway, blindly.

chapters.title: The Last Two Nights
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Final feasts: dishes of despair and of ending. Ada and Sera stop negotiating and start conspiring — using the taster's ritual itself, since a taster's approval binds the court's own law. Wren, fading, presses his hand to Ada's and gives him back the language fully. Emotional beat: resolve forged in exhaustion; the plan is thin and their faith is not.

chapters.title: The Ninth Dish
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Climax part one. On the ninth night the court serves a dish meant to end Wren permanently, requiring the taster's formal assent. Instead Ada declares it poisoned — and by the ancient law of tasters, his word is sovereign. The court convulses against its own rules. Emotional beat: triumph inverted into chaos; the weapon was always his tongue.

chapters.title: Burning to Give Light
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax part two. The contract breaks, but the ember must go somewhere: back to the valley, or die here. Wren cannot carry himself across the border. Ada, whose body has spent a lifetime absorbing what should have killed him, takes the ember into himself and walks it home through Merek's ambush and the collapsing court. Emotional beat: transfiguration; duty and love finally point the same direction.

chapters.title: The Valley Remembers Magic
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, then omniscient. Ada crosses the border stone carrying the ember and lets it go — into the valley's soil, its springs, its bread ovens. Magic returns gently to a place built to refuse it. Wren, soul restored, becomes a child again in truth. Merek faces the crown; the king, cured, owes Ada a debt no throne can name. Emotional beat: release; the safe valley becomes a true home.

chapters.title: A Table Set for Three
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Epilogue. Ada resigns as royal taster — his immunity spent, his purpose changed — and opens a small kitchen at the valley's edge with Sera, where the border stone hums and travelers from both worlds come to eat. Wren sets the tables and teaches them words with no translation. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted; the last ember glows in ordinary things.
